segments.text: What's up, devs? Welcome back to the channel. This is GitHub trending today number 23. And today we've got 32 open- source projects blowing up on GitHub right now. Let's get started.
Local development with port numbers sucks. Port conflicts, forgotten ports, wrong apps on cache tabs. Monor repos make it worse. AI agents guess wrong
ports. Local host cookies bleed across apps. Browser history is chaotic. Versel Labs built portless to fix this. One
line in package.json. Portless myapp next dev. Now your app is at my app localhost 1355. Stable URLs, no conflicts.
Weather is a terminalbased weather display with ASKI animations. Shows animated rain, snow, thunderstorms,
lightning, airplanes, and dayight cycles synced to real-time weather from open.
Auto detects location via IP or accepts manual coordinates. Simulate weather conditions to test animations. Toggle
HUD for temperature, wind, and precipitation. Keyboard controls for refresh, animation speed, and pause.
ZeroClaw is a Rust rewrite of OpenClaw.
The binary is 3 megabytes and launches instantly compared to a NodeJS process that typically sits around 400 megabytes of RAM. Supports 22 AI providers including Claude, OpenAI, and OAMA.
Connects to Telegram, and Discord out of the box. File systems sandboxed with null bite and SIM link protection. Three autonomy levels, readonly, supervised, full. Deploy anywhere, swap anything.
Preparing for DevOps interviews sucks.
Alex spent a year interviewing at Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, collecting every question asked. He scraped glass door and blind for more. 106 real
interview questions from 60 companies organized by Linux, networking, Kubernetes, Docker, Git, CI/CD, security. Entry to senior level. Each
has video explanation and links to interactive terminal solving at prepare.sh.
Debugging slow queries but logging feels indirect. SQL tap gives you real-time visibility. Sits between your
application and Postgress SQL or MySQL parses the wire protocol to intercept every query transparently. No code changes. Just point your app to the
proxy port. Beautiful bubble tminal UI shows live queries with transaction tracking rows affected errors. Run
explain on any captured query from the TUI. Running multiple AI agents is chaos.
Cloud code in one terminal, Gemini in another, adergent deck fixes this. Terminal session manager built with Go and Bubble T. One dashboard for all AI agent sessions.
Claude Code, Gemini CLI, ADER, Codeex, any terminal tool. Universal, not locked to one AI. Instant session creation.
Hierarchical project organization with collapsible groups. Fuzzy Search Oat is a lightweight semantic UI component library with zero
dependencies. 8K by total for CSS and JavaScript. No framework, no build system, no npm. Include two files and
start coding. Semantic HTML elements are styled automatically without classes. A few dynamic components use web components with minimal JavaScript.
Includes buttons, forms, typography, layouts, tables, and navigation.
Your shads and buttons look great, but they're silent. Soundc fixes that. It's shaden for sound effects. Instead of
hunting for MP3s and writing messy audio hooks, install UI sounds exactly like you install components. Want a satisfying pop or success chime?
Run the CLI command. It drops the sound asset and code directly into your project. Premium tactile feel without leaving your terminal.
Fast Code is a code-based analysis framework using hierarchical asbased indexing across files, classes, functions, and documentation for eight
plus languages. Three-phase architecture for LLM codebased navigation. Web UI launches in under two minutes. CLI mode
for automation and FSU integration via Nanobot websocket bridge for conversational queries.
Mems search provides memory for AI agents using markdown files as the source of truth. Plain files, human readable, git friendly. Vector store is
a derived index that can be rebuilt anytime. Smart dduplication with SHA 256 content hashing. Unchanged content never
re-mbbeds. Fileatcher autoindexes on save and deletes stale chunks when files are removed.
Skill Compose is a platform for building AI agents through natural language descriptions. Describe what you want. It finds existing skills from the library,
drafts missing ones, and connects them automatically. Skills are versioned packages with contracts, references, rubrics, and helpers. Agents evolve from
execution traces and user feedback, review proposed changes, and accept rewrites.
Rodney is a CLI tool for browser automation that launches headless Chrome and keeps it running. Each command connects via websocket, performs an
action, and disconnects. Navigate pages, extract text and HTML, execute JavaScript, and capture screenshots and
PDFs from shell commands. Accessibility testing commands show screen reader output, find elements by accessible name, and query for roles.
Doing code review with claude code, but wonder if GitHub copilot or eder would spot different issues. Counselors lets
you ask all of them at once. CLI tool fans out the same prompt to multiple AI coding agents in parallel. Claude code, codeex, whatever you have installed.
Your main agent assembles context with relevant code and git history. Then counselors dispatches simultaneously and aggregates responses.
Goey toast is a react toast notification library built on sauner with framer motion animations.
Pill-shaped toasts morph into gooey blobs during state transitions. Five toast types with semantic colors.
promise toasts that automatically morph from loading to success or error and action buttons with label morphback
animation. Rich descriptions support strings or react components.
No magic is a collection of single file dependencyfree Python implementations of AI and ML algorithms. Every script
trains a model from scratch and performs inference with zero frameworks. No PyTorch, no TensorFlow, just pure Python. One file per algorithm,
completely self-contained. Runs in minutes on CPU without GPU. Comments provide guided walkthroughs focused on understanding.
Want to run LLM locally but don't know what your hardware can handle? LM fit right sizes models to your system.
Terminal tool detects RAM, CPU, GPU, VRAM, and compares against a database of 33 popular models. Tells you exactly which ones will run. Run LLM fit.
Interactive TUI shows system specs.
Scrollable model tables sorted by compatibility. Hardware detection reads RAM via CIS info. Counts CPU cores.
Islands Dark is a Vcode theme that ports Jet Brains Islands Dark UI. Features floating glass panels with glass effect borders simulating directional light.
Pill-shaped activity bar with glass inset shadows and circular selection indicator. Breadcrumb bar dims until hovered with smooth fade in. Status bar
text dims until hover brightens with transition. Tab close buttons fade on hover.
Vel is a desktop Gmail client built with Rust and Tori. Email sync to local SQLite. No servers, full offline access,
instant startup, low memory. Keyboard first with superhuman style shortcuts and a command pallet. AI integration.
Claude, GPT, Gemini for thread summaries, smart replies, and inbox search all cached locally. Smart inbox
with autocategorization. snooze, schedule, send, undo, send, and follow-up reminders. You know how code bases get gross?
Manual review catches maybe 10%. Someone built dopify to fix this. Health scanner for your code. Finds 19 types of
problems in Typescript React. 12 for Python. Score is weighted so big problems count more. It tracks state between scans. Mark stuff fixed or won't
fix. The badge updates next gives you highest priority issue. Fix it. Rescan, repeat.
Your AI coding agent is guessing about your codebase structure instead of knowing it. Rome Code just gave agents X-ray vision. Instant comprehension tool
with multi- language A parsing. Builds call graphs, import graphs, reference chains, shows exact architectural topology. Health scoring with weighted
geometric mean across cyclatic complexity, maintainability, modularity, test coverage, documentation.
Arcentica is an agentic system for solving Arc AGI problems that achieved 85.3% accuracy with Claude Opus 4.6.
Main agent analyzes input output grid examples and spawns up to 10 sub aents.
Sub aents write Python programs to solve patterns, tests them against examples, pick the best one, and run it on test inputs. Two independent attempts per
problem takes the best result. Costs about $7 per task, including retries.
Arkmark is a Mac OS bookmark manager built with Swift that recreates Arc browser sidebar organization. Attaches as a sidebar to any browser window.
Multiple workspaces with custom colors, nested folders with drag and drop, inline editing and search. Imports directly from Arc by parsing its local
JSON file. Preserving folder and spaces structure. Local first with bookmarks in a single JSON file on your Mac. No accounts, no cloud sync.
Doing SEO audits manually or paying for expensive tools when Claude Code could do comprehensive analysis in one command. Claude SEO gives Claude Code
professional SEO powers. 12 specialized subsklls with six parallel sub aents working simultaneously during full
audits. Technical SEO EAT content quality schema markup AI search optimization for Google's generative engine.
Hibiki zero is a 3B parameter real-time speech translation model from Qout Labs that preserves the speaker's voice while
translating French, Spanish, Portuguese, and German to English. Simultaneous translation, no waiting for sentences to
finish. Adapts flow based on accumulated context. No word level aligned training data required. Runs on 8 to 12 gig VRAM, 3x faster than realtime on H100.
Visual explainer is an agent skill that turns messy terminal output into styled HTML pages you'll actually want to
share. No more asky art diagrams or broken table formatting. Ask your coding agent for an architecture overview, diff
or plan audit, and it generates a self-contained HTML page with real typography, dark mode, interactive mermaid diagrams with zoom and pan.
What if your GitHub repo could just run itself like handle its own issues, write its own status reports, do its own code reviews on a schedule while you sleep?
That's GitHub agentic workflows. It's from GitHub next. You write a markdown file in plain English, slap some front matter on it to say when it runs and
what it's allowed to touch, and the CLI converts that into a GitHub actions workflow powered by an AI agent.
Comfy UI OpenClaw adds remote control and automation to a local Comfy UI setup. Outbound only connector. No
firewall changes needed. Control generation jobs via web hooks, scheduled runs, or Telegram Discord. Approve or reject jobs remotely. Prompt planner
prompt refiner image to prompt batch varants. Supports multiple API providers with automatic failover.
Ironclaw is a Rust rewrite of OpenClaw, a self-hosted AI assistant that runs locally with no telemetry. Security is
the core focus. Tools run in W wasam sandboxes with capability based permissions. Secrets are injected at the host boundary and never exposed to tools
directly. HTTP requests are limited to an allow list. Prompt injection is handled through pattern detection and content sanitization.
Freeflow is an open- source Mac OS dictation app. Hold Fen anywhere to record. Release to paste the transcription into whatever field you're
typing in. It reads context from the active window. If you're replying to an email, it picks up names from the thread
and spells them correctly. If you're in a terminal, it treats input as code.
Processing happens locally. Nothing sent to FreeFlow servers.
Sandstorm runs clawed agent SDK instances in isolated cloud sandboxes.
Each agent gets a throwaway VM with full bash access. The agent can install packages, fetch web data, write files, and run scripts. The sandbox
self-destructs when finished. Send a post request with a prompt. Everything streams back in real time. No state leakage between runs.
Login machine is a single agent loop that handles any website login flow.
Credential forms, SSO pickers, MFA prompts, magic links, cookie banners. It takes a screenshot, strips the HTML down
to form relevant elements, and classifies the screen. Each screen type gets handled the same way by the same code. Your credentials go directly into the browser DOM.
Clawbox is a two command setup for running OpenClaw in a Mac OS tray. You get a fully provisioned Mac OS VM with OpenClaw installed, SSH configured, and
sensible defaults. Optional flags add Playright, Tail Scale, or other tools.
Developer mode mounts local source and runs multiple VMs concurrently with different openclaw checkpoints. One command to recreate, one to check status.
